svg.font-family: DM Sans, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: Inside the Watchdog: three steps, one findings table, alerts and an app
One job per region, running as you or as a Watchdog service principal. Steps 1 and 2 gather evidence; step 3 writes the one table that alerts (Phase 3) and the app (Phase 4) read.
WATCHDOG · ONE JOB PER REGION · ON DEMAND IN PHASE 1, SCHEDULED FROM PHASE 2
Read system tables
one SQL query covers every workspace in the region
WHAT YOU GET

g.text: • every job and run, in every workspace of the region

svg.text: BEST FOR
coverage, missed schedules, history and trends
About an hour behind. Runs over an hour are split into hourly rows,
and result_state is only on the last row.
Call each workspace's Jobs API
live detail, one call per workspace host

g.text: # every monitored job, in every workspace host

svg.text: REST: jobs/runs/list · jobs/runs/get · jobs/runs/get-output
WHAT YOU GET

g.text: • the run right now: life_cycle_state (QUEUED, RUNNING,
• start and end time, so how long it has been running
• every task: task_key, state, and attempt for retries
• the real error for a failed task: message and stack trace
• run_page_url, a direct link for the alert

svg.text: BEST FOR
live checks: failed tasks, even inside a
running job, long runs, retry loops
Needs CAN VIEW on each job, for you or the service principal.
API states differ from system tables (SUCCESS vs SUCCEEDED),
so the Watchdog normalizes them before writing.
Check, then write findings to one UC table
<catalog>.watchdog.findings · one row per job and check, every scan
CHECKS
config: your job list, owners and dependency map

g.text: • task failed, even inside a running job
• missed its schedule (no run in the window)
• later: stuck batch or no new data (Phase 2)
• later: service probes, such as Kafka (Phase 2)
• upstream impact: list the downstream jobs

svg.text: Writes safely
appends every scan, keyed by scan, job and check,
so a re-run never duplicates rows
FINDINGS TABLE COLUMNS
status: HEALTHY · WARNING · FAILED · UNKNOWN · source: SYSTEM_TABLES or JOBS_API
← dependency map
EXAMPLE ROWS (ILLUSTRATIVE)
observed_at, scan_id, job_name, check_id, status and source are on every row.
Alerts from the findings table · Phase 3
Databricks SQL alerts run a query on a schedule and notify
Slack, email, Teams, PagerDuty or a webhook.

g.text: orders_ingest fails: one alert naming the jobs it breaks
a continuous job stays on one batch ID with no new data
fails since the last scan: error text and run link
no run in the expected window
Kafka or an API down; names the jobs using it
the Watchdog could not check a job (UNKNOWN)
back to HEALTHY: one closing message

svg.text: ROUTING
Critical → PagerDuty · Warning → Slack, tagged to
the job owner · Recovery → a closing message
Alert on changes only:
compare each finding with the
previous one for the same job and check, so a failure alerts once.
A workspace admin sets up the notification destinations.
Watchdog app · Phase 4
a Databricks App that reads the same findings table

g.text: • Health now: every workspace and job, green, amber or red
• Incidents: open and resolved, with task drill-down,
error text and the run link
• Impact: what else breaks when orders_ingest fails
• Coverage: which jobs are watched, last scan, gaps
• Summary: last 12 or 24 hours, on demand
• Across workspaces: spot the same failure everywhere
• Later: acknowledge, add triage notes, and ask

svg.text: Planned for Phase 4. A good first version shows
health, incidents and the summary.
query
reads
